_: Riverwalk life-group and household sheet (2.5c), from the place record's life block.

norms.text: Reed mattresses are aired every dry morning.
Herbs from the cove shore are sorted into bundles before the evening meal.
Trodh is eaten alive at the long house table; Hassk-Nasha holds to it.

taboos.text: Wearing mud onto the long house floor.

values.text: Guests who sleep well and pay.

contempts.text: The shouting at the spit after dark.

place.text: The long house stands on piles in the shallows; the family has kept it a long time.

danger.text: If the cove silted up, the boats would go elsewhere and the long house would stand empty.

faction.text: The toll is no business of the household's, but its noise is.

addressTerms.text: Guest, for whoever is sleeping under the roof.

neverSaid.text: What a guest said in their sleep.

grievances.text: The toll argument keeps the guests awake.
